analysis_md:
# GIB — CGI Inc.
Engine 5.4 pass-1 run, 2026-10-16. Market cap $17,508,213,124 at $75.573 (nasdaq_quote_api) — in scope under $40B. All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json, or the cited company releases — none are recomputed.

## What it is
One of the largest independent IT and business consulting services firms in the world (94,000 consultants per company materials): strategic IT and business consulting, systems integration, managed IT and business-process services, and IP solutions, delivered through a local relationship model plus a global delivery network. Canadian IFRS filer (Form 40-F, fiscal year ends September 30), reporting in CAD; Class A subordinate voting shares trade directly on the NYSE as GIB and on the TSX as GIB.A — there is no ADS program (see ADS_RATIO flag below).

## Owner's earnings
**Latest year in the engine's EDGAR history is FY2024** (period ended 2024-09-30; USD, converted from CAD at period-end ECB rates — see FX flag): operating cash flow $1,631,334,622.72; capex $81,184,862.72; SBC $50,190,745.60 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2024: $1,499,959,014.40 = $6.47/share** (base_oe_latest_per_share $6.474470112405614).
- The maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC) is not printed for the recent history years in financials_history.csv (the ΔNWC leg is blank), so no maintenance figure is quoted — the OCF-based conservative series is used throughout.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years in the engine history. Net debt $907,904,273.92 plus lease liabilities of $458,771,084.80 at FY2024 (dcf_numbers.json); net debt is 0.66x normalized OE (diagnostics). Share count is shrinking 2.9%/yr (231,672,861 diluted in FY2024 vs 303,293,485 in FY2017).
- **Base used = normalized median of the last 3 FY OE/share: $5.93/share** (base_oe_per_share $5.93409291288451; the three median years are FY2022 $4.97, FY2023 $5.93, FY2024 $6.47 in financials_history.csv). The median is the conservative choice against the latest FY's $6.47 and is retained deliberately because the fresher data that would replace it is not yet in the computed outputs (see STALE_FY).

**Staleness, stated plainly:** CGI has already reported FY2025 (release of 2025-11-05: revenue CAD 15.91B, +8.4% reported / +4.6% constant currency; cash provided by operating activities CAD 2,234.2M; net earnings CAD 1,658.3M; diluted EPS CAD 7.35; adjusted diluted EPS CAD 8.30) and Q3 FY2026 (revenue CAD 4.19B, +2.5% / +1.3% constant currency; net earnings CAD 465.2M; diluted EPS CAD 2.23; adjusted diluted EPS CAD 2.29; bookings CAD 4.20B; backlog CAD 31.79B, 1.9x revenue; TTM book-to-bill 108.1%). Those prints are directionally consistent with the median base — reported FY2025 diluted EPS was essentially flat year over year while adjusted EPS grew — but they are NOT in the engine's numbers: EDGAR companyfacts does not yet carry CGI's FY2025 40-F (filed 2025-12-17, period 2025-09-30), and fundamentals.json states this explicitly ("latest 40-F (period 2025-09-30) is not yet in EDGAR companyfacts — annual / quarterly rows, TTM flows and this dividends block stop at 2024-09-30"). This score is therefore a stale-base result and confidence is low; pass 2 / a refresh should re-run it once companyfacts catches up.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow
Justification: backlog at 1.9x revenue, >100% book-to-bill, long-term managed-services contracts and government incumbency give contracted visibility and some switching friction, and company-reported ROIC has stayed above the cost of capital (16.0% FY2023/FY2024) — but it is falling (13.6% FY2025), the model is labor-based and won by competitive bidding against Accenture-scale rivals, and AI automation threatens headcount-based services economics. Evidence note: fundamentals.json carries no roic_proxy series and no gross-margin series for this IFRS filer (operating income is untagged in companyfacts), so the ROIC evidence is CGI's own reported return on invested capital (13.6% FY2025, 16.0% FY2024, 16.0% FY2023, from the FY2025 results release) and its adjusted EBIT margin, which held at 16.4% in FY2025 vs 16.5% in FY2024 and 16.2% in FY2023. ROE in fundamentals.json ran 0.18–0.20 over FY2022–FY2024 (CAD basis).
- FOR: Backlog of CAD 31.79B at Q3 FY2026, 1.9x annual revenue, with trailing book-to-bill of 108.1% — multi-year contracted visibility; long-term managed-services and outsourcing contracts plus a local relationship model create real, if rebid-limited, switching friction; scale of 94,000 consultants with deep government-sector incumbency; adjusted EBIT margin held at 16.2–16.5% across FY2023–FY2025 and OE positive 5 of the last 5 engine-history years; company-reported ROIC above the cost of capital through the cycle.
- AGAINST: Labor-based model won through competitive bidding, with price pressure and rebid risk; no proprietary product or platform lock-in against Accenture-scale and lower-cost offshore rivals; AI automation is a structural threat to headcount-based economics (CGI's own MD&A flags failure to adapt offerings to AI as a risk to revenue and cash flow); company-reported ROIC falling, 16.0% → 13.6%; constant-currency growth is low-single-digit (Q3 FY2026 +1.3% cc) and client IT budgets are cyclical; serial acquisitions bring recurring restructuring/integration charges (FY2025 adjustments of CAD 213.2M net of tax).
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — 5.4 final run (2026-10-16)
Growth sanity check (written, per spec): the engine's blended OE/share growth start is 6.89% — its components are revenue CAGR 5y 3.50%, revenue CAGR 3y 4.48%, latest revenue YoY 2.00%, and OE/share CAGR 2y 14.11%, with revenue components adjusted +2.90pp for the shrinking share count. Against actual prints: FY2025 revenue grew +8.4% reported (+4.6% constant currency, acquisition-assisted) and adjusted diluted EPS +8.9%; FY2026 year-to-date revenue grew +4.4% (+2.1% cc) and Q3 adjusted diluted EPS +9.0%. OE/share growth in the mid-single digits is therefore the evidenced center, not revenue growth alone. Scenario starts were recalibrated DOWN from the default offsets at the top end only: the default bull (+5pp → 11.89%) and super-bull (+12pp → 18.89%) starts sit above every recent print including acquisition-boosted FY2025, so offsets were set to −12 / −5 / −1 / +4 / +8pp, giving starts of −5.11% / 1.89% / **5.89%** / 10.89% / 14.89%. The base start (5.89%) sits below the blend because constant-currency revenue growth is decelerating (+1.3% cc in Q3 FY2026); the super-bull start (14.89%) is a tail case requiring re-accelerating bookings plus continued buybacks, held at 10% probability. Probabilities are the defaults 10/25/30/25/10; OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $75.573.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | -5.1% | 0.75 | AI deflation plus a client-budget downturn cuts OE/share | $26.55 | 6.59% |
| Bear | 25% | 1.9% | 0.90 | Constant-currency stagnation sticks; margins slip | $42.70 | 9.54% |
| Base | 30% | 5.9% | 1.00 | Low-single-digit cc growth plus the buyback tailwind | $56.03 | 11.86% |
| Bull | 25% | 10.9% | 1.10 | AI/transformation demand re-accelerates bookings; margins hold | $75.75 | 15.03% |
| Super bull | 10% | 14.9% | 1.25 | Durable re-acceleration with M&A and buybacks compounding | $101.38 | 18.72% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $59.21 (−21.65% vs price), IV@12% $78.97, IV@10% $101.03, IV@20% $41.51, IV@25% $31.79, weighted IRR 12.41%, base-case IRR 11.86%**
- **Tier by numbers: C.** Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 7.85%, terminal value 19.11% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.82x, net debt 0.66x normalized OE, 24.5 months since the engine's latest FY end (the staleness is a companyfacts lag, not a filing lag — see STALE_FY).

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 25 months ago): the FY2025 40-F was filed 2025-12-17 but is not yet in EDGAR companyfacts, so the engine history and fundamentals.json both stop at FY2024 (fundamentals.json says so in its own notes). ttm.py was run and exits non-zero for this IFRS filer — it reads us-gaap only and reports no annual facts — so no TTM base is available; per spec the median base ($5.93/share) is used and the result is labeled stale-base with confidence low. Reported FY2025/Q3 FY2026 prints (quoted in the OE section) are directionally consistent with that base.
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count shrinking 2.9%/yr): already credited via the +2.90pp growth adjustment in the blend; not double-counted in the verdict. Q3 FY2026 alone repurchased 4,427,600 Class A shares for CAD 412.9M per the quarterly release.
- **FX_CONVERTED** (CAD → USD at period-end ECB reference rates): flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json (FY2024: 0.73984 USD/CAD). Per-share figures are USD on this basis throughout.
- **ADS_RATIO_APPLIED** (preliminary run flagged ADS_RATIO_MISSING): resolved under bounded authority (d) — there is no ADS. The FY2025 Form 40-F cover registers "Class A subordinate voting shares" (GIB) on the New York Stock Exchange under Section 12(b); the NYSE-traded security IS the ordinary Class A share, so judgment.json carries ads_ratio {ratio: 1.0} with the filing as source. No per-share figure changes.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear-case tier D at 9.54% vs bull-case tier B at 15.03%): the verdict spans tiers; the final verdict below is sized to the bear end, per the flag.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the stale base: this is a Tier C print on FY2022–FY2024 economics. FY2025 as reported (adjusted EPS +8.9%, OCF CAD 2,234.2M on revenue +8.4%) would likely produce a similar-to-slightly-better base, not a different verdict — reported diluted EPS was flat and net earnings fell 2.0% in FY2025 on restructuring/integration charges, and FY2026 constant-currency growth has slowed to ~1–2%. A refresh once companyfacts ingests the FY2025 40-F is the first thing pass 2 should check.
- Quality is real but not wide-moat: two decades of disciplined compounding, backlog at 1.9x revenue, book-to-bill above 100%, margins pinned near 16% adjusted EBIT — against a falling ROIC (16.0% → 13.6%) and an industry whose headcount economics AI is actively repricing. That is a 5, not a 7.
- Balance sheet is not the story: net debt 0.66x normalized OE on the engine basis; the company-reported net debt rose in FY2025 (CAD 3,451.4M, 25.1% net debt to capitalization) on acquisition funding — worth watching, not thesis-breaking.
